added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed run's manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite arm (both null in its manifest and its classification.json), so an added-failure count is not derivable from the reviewed run's own gate logs

findings.text: follow-on: review_path's committed branch defaults a missing review_run_id to reviewed_run_id (name = str(review_run_id or "").strip() or reviewed_run_id) where its sibling plan_review_path refuses an empty review run id outright (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:383). The two owners of "a committed path" therefore disagree, and the default is the wrong one for a run review: a re-review is a new review run, so a caller that omits the id names the file after the reviewed run and a second review run of the same run overwrites the first rather than adding the new file the plan's rule intends. store_committed_review always supplies the id, so no production path hits it today, and the refusal case covers only the plan owner (tests/test_review_records_have_a_committed_root.py:130).

follow-on: run_record_times' live-pointer fallback — the branch taken when the run has no committed per-run record — is exercised by no test case, so the shape it assumes of the live pointer (created_at for dispatch, completed_at for completion) is unverified; a pointer carrying neither yields ("","") and the committed record then silently drops both stamps, which is exactly the store-clock substitution the committed tree exists to remove.

item_verdicts.call_sites: store_committed_review has no production caller yet — the wiring is owned by the sibling node state-write-commits-a-set-of-paths and the reviewed manifest discloses it; the pre-existing review_path/plan_review_path callers (reckon/cli.py:5529, reckon/crew/recovery.py:612/615/1018) are unchanged and omit committed_root, so they keep the staging path.

item_verdicts.done_when: The EVIDENCE measure names the four-module gate; I re-ran the new module at the reviewed head (6 passed, EXIT=0) and the full four-module gate (36 passed, EXIT=0), reproducing the recorded figure, and I reproduced the declared mutation in a scratch copy — dropping the response_events append reddens test_record_response_appends_events_and_keeps_the_body with 1 failed, EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal — a review record can be written to the project's committed docs/state reviews tree and its answers appended as events — is met: review_path (reckon/crew/review.py:1288) and plan_review_path (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:355) each gain a committed branch resolving docs/state/<project>/reviews/run/<reviewed-run-id>/<review-id>.json and …/plan/<slug>/<review-id>.json beside the unchanged staging path, store_committed_review (reckon/crew/review.py:1751) writes into that tree, and record_response appends to RESPONSE_EVENTS_KEY (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:960).
item_verdicts.manifest: Read at the run's manifest.md; it declares status complete, commit 2e05df719, the four-module gate with 36 passed EXIT=0, the response_events negative control (1 failed, EXIT=1), and discloses that the reader repointing, the ledger set-commit and the recovery hash-object -w remain owned by other nodes; its tests line names no baseline_suite or after_suite arm.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --stat 3c7a3f36a 2e05df719 is exactly the four paths the manifest declares — reckon/crew/review.py, reckon/crew/plan_review.py, tests/test_review_records_have_a_committed_root.py and docs/evidence/fragments/every-review-is-kept-as-a-committed-record/review-records-have-a-committed-root.html — 518 insertions against 4 deletions; no plan meta line or shared index is touched.

justifications.durability: the response_events half is guarded — I reproduced the declared mutation and it reddens test_record_response_appends_events_and_keeps_the_body (1 failed, EXIT=1) — and the committed path and time halves are held by exact-value assertions that fail on a wrong path or a defaulted clock, but no mutation arm covers those halves, run_record_times' live-pointer fallback is untested, and review_path's committed branch carries no refusal case.
justifications.evidence: the gate is recorded (gate.log, 36 passed in 32.01s, EXIT=0) and I reproduced both the four-module gate (36 passed) and the negative control (1 failed, EXIT=1) at the reviewed head; but the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so added failures are unmeasured and the new checks are not shown to discriminate beyond the one declared mutation.
justifications.fit: the change extends the existing path owners (review_path, plan_review_path), the docs-dir resolver (_store._docs_dir_for_project) and the existing store, and the new symbols are named by behaviour (committed_review_root, run_record_times, store_committed_review, RESPONSE_EVENTS_KEY) with no plan, ticket or version label in the diff.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the three claims the goal names all hold at head — both path owners resolve the committed tree beside the staging path, a committed record carries the run's dispatch and completion times rather than the store clock, and a response appends an event while the responses map keeps the latest answer — matching the goal as stated.
justifications.reuse: committed_review_root reuses _store._docs_dir_for_project rather than inventing a docs lookup, the committed branch lives on the existing review_path/plan_review_path rather than a second path rule, and store_committed_review reuses _write_record; grep finds no forked path owner or second writer.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 3c7a3f36a 2e05df719 is four files and 518 insertions against 4 deletions, every one inside the declared write paths, with no plan meta line or shared index touched.
